block.name: Burst Time Tagger CC
block.doc:
Burst-based tx_time tagger for USRP experiments.
The block takes a complex stream and:
- passes it to the output unchanged, - periodically marks bursts of "Burst length (samples)", - for each burst, adds: * tx_time (UHD tuple {full_sec, frac_sec}), * tx_sob at the first sample, * tx_eob at the last sample.
Timing model:
Let: - samp_rate : sample rate in Hz, - period_s : active period between bursts (seconds), - gap_s : extra gap appended after each period (seconds), - offsets : list of offsets (seconds) where each burst starts inside each active period, - t0_usrp : UHD time (seconds) of sample index 0, - lead_s : additional lead in seconds.
For a burst starting at absolute sample index burst_start:
t_burst = t0_usrp + burst_start / samp_rate + lead_s
The block converts t_burst into {full_sec, frac_sec} and writes a tx_time tag at the beginning of the burst, together with tx_sob, and a tx_eob tag at the last sample.
Control message port:
The block has an input message port "ctrl". It expects a PMT dictionary that may contain:
- "t0_usrp" : double (UHD time in seconds), - "lead_s" : double (lead in seconds).
When a valid control message is received, the block updates its internal t0_usrp and/or lead_s and sets an internal flag so that burst tagging only starts after the control message is applied. Before that, the block acts as a pure pass-through without any tags.
Parameters:
- Sample rate (Hz) [samp_rate]: Must match the USRP sink sample rate.
- Active period (s) [period_s]: Duration of the active region where bursts live (e.g. 10 ms).
- Gap after period (s) [gap_s]: Extra idle time after the active part. Effective period is (period_s + gap_s).
- Burst length (samples) [burst_len]: Number of samples inside each burst.
- Initial USRP time (s) [t0_usrp]: Initial guess for t0_usrp (seconds). This can be later refined via the "ctrl" message from another block.
- Offsets (s) [offsets]: Python list of offsets in seconds inside each period where each burst starts. For a single burst per period, use [0.0].
- Lead ahead (s) [lead_s]: Additional lead added to t_burst for tx_time tag computation.
Runtime configuration:
All parameters have associated callbacks and can be updated from GNU Radio Companion while the flowgraph is running.
